skill.name: starknet-wallet
skill.description: Guide AI agents through Starknet balance checks, token transfers, contract calls, session keys, and gasless transactions.
skill.summary: Operate Starknet wallets with balance, transfer, contract, paymaster, and session-key guidance.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, template literals, placeholder secrets, and expected RPC configuration. Confirmed risks include an import outside the audited tree and direct signing-key use. Semantic review also identified irreversible transactions and autonomous session-key spending.

remediation.issue: The RPC version helper imports code from outside the audited skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Copy the helper into this skill or package it as a pinned dependency, then include it in security scanning and integrity checks.

remediation.issue: A documented workflow gives agent code direct access to STARKNET_PRIVATE_KEY.
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated signer or hardware-backed wallet. Prefer scoped session keys, and prevent private-key values from entering prompts, logs, or tool output.

remediation.issue: Transfer, swap, approval, and contract-invocation workflows can move assets irreversibly.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation with recipient, token, amount, fees, contract, entrypoint, calldata summary, and simulation results before submission.

remediation.issue: Session keys can authorize repeated transactions without per-action approval.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce contract and method allowlists, low spending limits, short expiry, revocation procedures, and transaction monitoring for every session key.

content.value_statement: Starknet wallet workflows require careful handling of balances, fees, and signing credentials. This skill guides agents through queries, transfers, contract calls, and session-key controls.
actual_capabilities: Checks one Starknet token balance by symbol or contract address.
Queries several token balances through a BalanceChecker contract with RPC fallback.
Guides token transfers, fee estimates, swaps, and gasless paymaster options.
Explains read-only calls, state-changing contract invocations, and multi-call transactions.
Shows session-key policies for contract access, spending limits, expiry, and revocation.
Provides TypeScript scripts for single-token and multi-token balance checks.
limitations: Requires a working Starknet RPC endpoint and compatible Starknet and AVNU SDK versions.
Does not provide wallet custody, key storage, or a deployed MCP server.
State-changing actions require a secure signer and independent transaction confirmation.
External providers, token metadata, paymaster services, and contract addresses can change.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Wallet Workflows
use_cases.description: Add balance checks, transfers, fee estimation, and confirmation gates to an AI agent.

use_cases.title: Monitor Treasury Balances
use_cases.description: Review ETH, STRK, USDC, and USDT balances before funding or payment operations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Contract Transactions
use_cases.description: Plan read calls, approvals, invocations, multi-calls, and gasless execution with clear safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Check Wallet Balances
prompt_templates.prompt: Check ETH, STRK, USDC, and USDT balances for [wallet address]. Explain the result without performing any transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a [token] transfer of [amount] to [recipient]. Estimate fees, verify balance, and request confirmation before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Contract Call
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Starknet call: [contract, entrypoint, calldata]. Identify asset movement, approvals, fees, and failure conditions before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Session-Key Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a least-privilege session-key policy for [workflow], with allowlists, spending limits, expiry, revocation, and monitoring requirements.

output_examples.input: Check ETH and USDC balances for the specified Starknet wallet.
Prepare a transfer of 25 STRK and stop before signing.
output_examples.output: The transfer plan lists the recipient, amount, available balance, estimated fee, and confirmation request. No transaction is signed.

output_examples.input: Create a session-key policy for recurring USDC payments.
output_examples.output: The policy limits contracts, methods, payment size, total spending, duration, and revocation. It also requires monitoring and alerts.

best_practices: Validate network, recipient, token address, amount, balance, and fee before every state-changing action.
Use isolated signers and short-lived session keys with strict method and spending limits.
Simulate contract calls and show a complete transaction summary before requesting confirmation.
anti_patterns: Do not place private keys in prompts, logs, source files, or tool responses.
Do not submit transfers, swaps, approvals, or contract calls without explicit user confirmation.
Do not grant broad session-key permissions without allowlists, spending limits, expiry, and revocation.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Starknet wallet?
faq.answer: It provides wallet workflow guidance and examples. Account creation depends on the Starknet tooling available in your environment.

faq.question: Can it transfer tokens?
faq.answer: Yes. Every transfer should require recipient validation, fee review, balance checks, secure signing, and explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Which tokens are supported?
faq.answer: Examples cover ETH, STRK, USDC, and USDT. Other tokens can use verified symbols or contract addresses.

faq.question: Does it support gasless transactions?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers AVNU paymaster workflows and token-based gas payment where supported.

faq.question: How are private keys handled?
faq.answer: The examples reference environment variables. Production use should rely on isolated signers or tightly scoped session keys.

faq.question: Can it call any Starknet contract?
faq.answer: It explains generic contract calls. Users must verify contract addresses, entrypoints, calldata, approvals, fees, and expected state changes.
